name: Coastline to Negev Corridor
inspired_by: Israel in 2026, compressed north to south into one fictional map: the Upper Galilee hills along the Lebanese border, the densely built central coastal plain, and the northern Negev desert with agricultural communities near the Gaza perimeter. Mixed Jewish, Arab and Bedouin communities are represented with fictional towns; no real city is reproduced.
climate: Mediterranean in the north and on the coast (Koppen Csa: 600-900 mm rain in the Galilee, 450-550 mm on the coast), grading to semi-arid and arid in the Negev (BSh/BWh: 100-250 mm). Summers 30-36 C on the coast and plain, 38-42 C in the Negev; winters mild, with frost and rare snow on the Galilee ridges.
seasons: Winter (Dec-Feb): rain fronts and green hills in the north and centre, flash floods in Negev wadis
Spring (Mar-May): wildflowers, hot sharav/hamsin desert winds with dust, wheat harvest in the south
Summer (Jun-Sep): dry and humid on the coast, very hot and dry inland, brush fires
Autumn (Oct-Nov): first rains, olive harvest in the Galilee, citrus season starts

vegetation: apple and cherry orchards on high ground
citrus and avocado orchards between towns
acacia (Vachellia tortilis, V. raddiana) in wadi beds
bare reg (desert pavement) and chalk badlands

terrain.relief: North: steep limestone and basalt hills to about 1,050 m with deep valleys. Centre: flat to gently rolling coastal plain (0-80 m) behind beaches and low sandstone (kurkar) ridges. South: loess plain at 50-250 m cut by gullies, rising to chalk and flint hills and a small erosion cirque in the south-east corner.
features: kurkar sandstone ridges parallel to the coast
loess gullies (badlands) in the northern Negev
wide braided wadi beds with acacias
a small erosion cirque (makhtesh-type) with colourful sandstone
border fence and security road along the north and south-west edges
terrain.water: Mediterranean along the west edge; one small perennial river on the coastal plain with a reed-lined estuary; seasonal Negev wadis prone to winter flash floods; water reservoirs, fish ponds and the national water carrier canal and pipeline crossing north to south.

generator.approach: Heightmap at 10 m resolution with three latitude bands blended over 2 km transitions (north hills, centre plain, south loess/desert). Each band uses its own noise mix; a coast distance field flattens the west edge and adds a dune strip; wadis carved by flow accumulation in the south band only.

noise_layers.purpose: Galilee hill mass, masked to the north band
kurkar ridges parallel to the coast in the centre band
Negev rise and chalk hills, masked to the south band

generator.erosion: Strong hydraulic erosion in the south band (loess gullies), light elsewhere; thermal erosion capped at 40 degrees in the cirque walls.
generator.rivers: One coastal river spline with estuary; Negev wadis from flow accumulation, broad flat beds (20-200 m) with gravel, dry except in flash-flood weather events.
generator.settlement_flattening: City districts flattened to 2-5 m benches; hill villages per plot; kibbutzim and moshavim flattened as one disc with a 100 m skirt.
generator.notes: The centre band is very dense and suits only small contract zones. The north and south bands host the larger zones. The national highway and rail run north-south through all three bands and form the convoy spine.

settlements.architecture: Coastal-plain city: four- to nine-storey apartment blocks on pilotis (open ground floors), white and cream plaster, many balconies, flat roofs with solar water heaters, newer 15-30 storey towers; every apartment has a reinforced-concrete safe room (one thick-walled room per unit). Older core of white-plaster modernist houses; shopping streets with awnings; public shelters marked in parks.
settlements.wall_class: Concrete frames thick; block infill thin; safe rooms 20-30 cm reinforced concrete thick (best cover in a building); glass shopfronts no cover.
layout_rules: grid streets with a boulevard and a central bus station
malls and a market hall as landmarks
parks with public shelters
multi-lane ring road and an industrial zone on the edge
very high civilian density

settlements.architecture: Galilee Arab town on a hillside: three- to five-storey family houses of concrete, built floor by floor for grown children, stone cladding, arched windows, flat roofs with water tanks and rebar stubs; a mosque and a church; narrow steep lanes. Also development towns of 1950s-1960s four-storey housing blocks.
settlements.wall_class: Concrete frames thick; infill thin; stone cladding medium.
layout_rules: organic on slopes, main street along the contour
old core with stone houses and a market
new neighbourhoods spreading uphill
few vehicle entries; steep pedestrian stairs

settlements.architecture: Kibbutz and moshav agricultural communities: one-storey houses with red-tile or flat roofs and gardens, a dining hall, a water tower, cowsheds, chicken coops, packing houses, a perimeter fence with a security gate and patrol road; each house has a safe room. Border-adjacent communities have extra fences and concrete shelters at bus stops.
settlements.wall_class: Houses block or prefab thin, except the safe room thick; shelters thick concrete.
layout_rules: ring road inside a perimeter fence
central lawn with dining hall and water tower
fields, orchards and greenhouses outside the fence
single main gate plus agricultural gates
eucalyptus windbreak

settlements.architecture: Negev Bedouin town and unrecognised villages: planned neighbourhoods of two-storey concrete houses, plus dispersed hamlets of tin and block shacks, tents and livestock pens without grid utilities; solar panels and water tanks.
settlements.wall_class: Concrete houses medium; shacks and tents no cover.
layout_rules: planned town in neighbourhood clusters with wide roads
unrecognised hamlets scattered on hillsides with dirt tracks
livestock pens and water tanks

settlements.architecture: Military bases and installations: fenced bases with hangar sheds and barracks, air-defence battery sites on hills, a desert airbase with hardened shelters (aircraft AI only), border observation posts with camera towers.
settlements.wall_class: Shelters and berms thick; prefabs thin.
layout_rules: perimeter fence and patrol road
hilltop placement for observation and air defence
single main gate with barrier and guard post

infrastructure.roads: A north-south six-lane motorway and a parallel older highway; dense urban roads in the centre; winding two-lane roads in the Galilee; straight desert highways and a border security road in the south.
infrastructure.rail: Electrified double-track line north-south with stations in the city district and a branch to the Negev; elevated sections and level crossings.
infrastructure.power: Gas-fired power station on the coast, high-voltage lines inland, a large solar field in the Negev.
infrastructure.ports: One commercial port and marina on the central coast (LHD approach), a desalination plant beside it.
infrastructure.airfields: Desert airbase in the south (AI aircraft only, out of bounds), a small civil airfield on the coast.
infrastructure.checkpoints: Few internal checkpoints; gates at communities and bases; border crossings for goods at the south-west edge (Gaza perimeter) closed or restricted; army checkpoints along the northern border road during escalations.

pois.contract_use: counter-drone site defence; protect from rocket teams

pois.description: Agricultural community 2-3 km from the south-west perimeter: houses with safe rooms, dining hall, water tower, a security fence and a cowshed; partly evacuated.
pois.contract_use: escort returning residents; infrastructure repair escort; infiltration-alert defence

pois.description: Observation post on a ridge above the northern border: concrete tower, camera masts, bunker, fence and patrol road; overlooking terraced villages across the line.
pois.contract_use: recover a downed drone on the slope; observation post resupply under fire

pois.description: Coastal power station with turbine halls, chimneys, a coal jetty, fuel tanks and a fenced switchyard.
pois.contract_use: protect infrastructure from drone attack; repair-crew escort

pois.description: Desalination plant by the port: long membrane halls, intake pipes, tank farm and a control building.
Multi-level motorway interchange with overpasses, concrete sound walls, a gas station and a logistics centre.

pois.description: Pine forest on a ridge with fire breaks, an old stone watchtower and a lookout parking area; drone launch debris after attacks.
pois.contract_use: recover a downed drone; search for an infiltrating cell; brush-fire hazard

pois.description: Negev wadi with acacias and tracks leading to the southern border, abandoned vehicle and drop point. Weapons and drug smuggling interdiction site.

pois.description: Truck inspection yard near the south-west crossing: scanners, warehouses, rows of lorries, a fenced staging area.
pois.contract_use: escort aid convoy; secure the yard during a protest or attack

pois.description: Industrial park with warehouses, a defence-electronics plant, workshops and loading docks.

pois.description: Rim of a desert erosion cirque with a visitor centre, switchback road and cliffs; deep valley floor with coloured sands.
pois.contract_use: downed-aircrew or drone recovery in rough terrain; navigation training

pois.description: Fenced base with vehicle sheds, barracks, a helipad, maintenance hangars and a fuel point.

conditions: winter storms with heavy rain and hail
morning fog on the coastal plain
weather.visibility_notes: Hamsin dust days drop visibility to 500 m-2 km across the south; winter storms ground helicopters for hours; urban areas are lit all night, so NVGs bloom.
weather.dust_or_snow: Dust in spring and autumn in the Negev; snow only on the highest Galilee ridges, rarely.

civilians.behaviour: Dense, busy population in the centre at all hours; heavy commuter traffic 07:00-09:00 and 16:00-19:00; Friday afternoon to Saturday evening quieter streets in Jewish towns, Friday busier in Arab towns. Alert sirens send civilians to safe rooms and public shelters within 15-90 seconds, emptying streets; northern and Gaza-perimeter communities may be partly evacuated during escalations. Farm workers in fields at dawn.
civilians.casualty_risk_notes: The highest civilian density of any theatre with israel_gaza: almost every fight in the centre band risks the 8-casualty void. The game should keep zones in the hills, desert and community perimeters.

factions_present.where: Whole map: bases, air-defence batteries, border posts on the north and south-west edges, community security teams; patrols on the border roads.
North edge only: drone launches and ATGM teams across the border ridge, rare infiltration attempts into the Galilee forest ridges.
South-west edge only: perimeter infiltration attempts toward border communities, drone and rocket fire as map events.
South-west edge only: small rocket teams across the perimeter as map events; rare small cells.

frontline: Static borders, dynamic threat. The persistent war here is mostly fire across the edges: escalation events from hezbollah (north) or hamas and pij (south-west) raise the alert level in border zones, evacuate communities, and post counter-drone, infrastructure-protection and drone-recovery contracts for isr. Ceasefire events lower it and post return-of-residents and repair-escort contracts. No zone inside the map is held by the non-state groups; they only appear as small infiltrating teams or as map hazards (rocket and drone strikes, game-level).
contract_hooks: Counter-drone site defence at an air-defence battery or power station (client isr)
Recover a downed drone from a northern border slope under observation (client isr)
Protect a desalination plant or power station from drone and rocket teams (client isr)
Intel recovery on weapons smuggling in a Negev wadi (client isr)
Escort an aid convoy from the logistics yard to the crossing (client isr; neutral humanitarian framing)
Escort residents returning to a partly evacuated border community (client isr)
Hostage or remains-recovery intel lead follow-up in the perimeter area (client isr; intel only, no strike missions)

contract_zones.name: Coastal infrastructure
contract_zones.notes: counter-drone, adjacent to very dense city

hot_zones.name: Galilee border escalation
hot_zones.layout: No enemy HQ on the map: the 'HQ' is across the border edge. 4 enemy launch and observation sites as outposts near the edge, isr checkpoints on ridge roads, roaming isr patrols, 2 drone-attack waves per hour; the player defends sites and recovers assets

insertion.fob: LHD offshore for coastal contracts (via the commercial port). Inland FOB at a host-nation army base in the northern Negev for southern and northern contracts; helicopter transport only in hot zones, and civilian airspace makes AI flights take set corridors (proposed).

early_game_notes: Not terrorist-heavy on the map itself: the non-state factions appear only at the edges at low strength. Mostly mid-campaign defensive and recovery contracts for a neutral client.
ambient_audio: call to prayer and church bells in Galilee towns
desert wind and silence in the Negev
